newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro doomed to rapid failure - France's Calvet.
newsitem.headline: Euro doomed to rapid failure - France's Calvet.

text.p: Jacques Calvet, chairman of carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen and an outspoken critic of European monetary union, said the euro was bound to collapse because of a lack of policy coordination in member countries.
"I'm persuaded that in three months, six months, a year (after its creation), there will be serious crises and the euro will collapse," he told radio RTL.

The French government is one of the driving forces behind the establishment of a single currency, set to be launched in 1999. European Union countries will decide next year which countries will join in the first wave of monetary union.

Calvet said the euro "will be destroyed because we won't be able to hold fixed parities among the different countries adopting the euro as long as economic, social, fiscal and financial policies vary from one country to the next".
"We don't have a foundation allowing for the lasting establishment of a single currency," he said.
"We've put the cart before the horse, and I'm not sure we have horses," Calvet said.
He said a single European currency would eventually be "desirable, even indispensable" but requires that "we have the same vision of the future in all the countries making up the European Union".
